question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}(x-2),\, & 3\le x\le 4 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<3 \\ h(x),\, & 3\le x\le 4 \\ 1,\, & x>4.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$

current_example.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $0 \leq x \leq 12,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14128904/assets/26f067fb119dcd38dd41d27bbd5a6ceb019b8f40055cff9949f150adb6f7c562.svg)

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{1}{72}t\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={\frac{1}{144}{t}^{2}|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{144}{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by
